source.title: Functional neurological restoration of amputated peripheral nerve using biohybrid regenerative bioelectronics

material: PEDOT:PSS microelectrode array on parylene C with fibrin hydrogel and iPSC-derived myocytes (biohybrid device)

formulation.evidence: Final concentrations are as follows: FG = 3.125, 6.25, 12.5, and 25 mg/ml; Th = 1 U/ml; and CaCl2 = 20 mM.

processing.evidence: The solution is spin-coated three times with soft bakes for 60 s at 120°C.
After the final spin-coat, there is a hard bake for 1 hour at 130°C.
A 2-μm-thick parylene C layer was deposited on silicon wafers
The devices are plasma-treated at 25 W for 1 min to make the surface hydrophilic for cell culture.

electrode_area.evidence: MEA occupied a 2-mm by 2-mm area within the larger parylene device

biology.cell_type: human iPSC-derived skeletal myocytes; host rat forearm nerve (ulnar and median)

culture_days.evidence: mature multinucleated myotubes are formed on the surface of the biohybrid device by day 8

other_outcomes.evidence: implanted human iPSC-derived myocytes can survive in a rat model for up to 28 days
other_outcomes.name: in vivo cell survival duration

other_outcomes.evidence: weeks 1 to 4: 12.9-, 11.3-, 19.7-, and 32.0-dB mean signal￾to-noise ratio (SNR), respectively
other_outcomes.name: SNR week 4 awake recording

other_outcomes.evidence: They were seeded onto devices with densities of 100,000 cells/cm2
other_outcomes.name: cell seeding density

notes: Impedance measured at 1000 Hz in DPBS, three-electrode configuration; yield 97% before seeding and 25% at week 4 in vivo. Implanted 4 weeks in immunodeficient rats.
